meta.title: Mandarin Chinese — First phrases
meta.subtitle: 80 replies, days and first questions made of Level 1's words — beside Level 1
meta.desc: 80 things a beginner can already say with Level 1's words, none of them a card in any other deck here: the replies (不是, 没问题, 太好了), the days of the week (the syllabus lists only 星期 and Sunday), last and next week and month, the plain negatives (不会, 不能, 不在), a few numbers, people, and everyday actions (吃饭, 回家, 买东西) — and 5 whole first questions and answers (你叫什么名字？ 这个多少钱？). Every one is written only with characters the Level 1 deck uses. 80 notes, each with TWO cards — Chinese → English and English → Chinese — each scheduled on its own. THE ORDER is a teaching order: replies and courtesies, the first questions, the days, time, asking and saying no, counting, people, actions, places. Study it beside or after Level 1; at the default of ten new cards a day, both directions together, it takes 16 days. — The card is the vocabulary decks' card: simplified and traditional forms, pinyin, bopomofo, the meaning, each character broken into its parts, and up to three example sentences with a speaker. The pinyin writes 一 and 不 with the tone they are said with (bú shì, yí ge), as the Level 1 deck does; the bopomofo keeps the dictionary's tone. 24 of the 75 phrases have no short example sentence in the decks and show none. — WHAT IS NOT HERE: anything the dictionary has no entry for. 你好吗, 多少钱 on its own, 不知道, 好的 and 我爱你 are not CC-CEDICT headwords, so they are not carded; the 5 sentences are here because the Level 1 deck already carries each of them, with its translation. Nothing was composed. — Headwords, traditional forms and meanings: CC-CEDICT, release of 2026-11-15 (CC BY-SA 4.0), its senses quoted unaltered. Character parts and their meanings: Make Me a Hanzi. Sentences and their translations: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, as carried by the HSK 3.0 decks on this shelf.
